claim: The 28 plan models are checked only against 812 cells copied from the kernel's own output (637 values, 97 not_applicable, 78 errors) at rel 2e-3. A defect present when the goldens were recorded, or introduced and re-recorded, passes: no relation between the values is asserted for these aircraft.
evidence:
for slug, golden in GOLDEN[member].items():
        check(by_slug[slug], golden)   # check(): assert close(quantity.value, golden) with REL = 2e-3
recommended_test: Aero tier, same file, reusing the one compute per member: for every member whose values are floats assert (a) stall-speed < minimum-sink-speed < minimum-drag-speed; (b) stall-speed == sqrt(2 m g / (rho S_ref C_L,max)) with m = member.mass_kg, g = 9.80665, rho = 1.225 kg/m^3, S_ref = member.asb_reference[0], rel 2e-3; (c) per world sign(spiral-criterion-x) == -sign(spiral-doubling-time-x) for x in md, mp, app; (d) neutral-point worlds lie between the main wing's quarter-chord MAC x and the tail's quarter-chord MAC x for members of WITH_PITCH_TAIL. (a)-(c) hold for all recorded goldens today (checked by importing GOLDEN), so nothing is weakened.

The suite is green while the defect exists, and a new internal error can be recorded the same way without anyone deciding it.
evidence:

Keep the existing golden test unchanged.

claim: Goldens are re-recorded by hand-pasting numbers into the test files; there is no recorder, no update flag and no generated old/new report. The six MVP files keep manual '#1358: was ...' comments, the plan batch keeps none, and the seven AVL snapshots in reference/snapshots have no regeneration script. A regeneration can bless a regression with nothing but the PR diff of ~800 floats as the gate.
recommended_test: Add scripts/canon_checks/reference_fleet/record_goldens.py (aero tier, run through the lock) that computes the fleet and writes a JSON golden file plus a report listing, per aircraft and slug, old value, new value and relative change, and status changes (ok -> error and back) first. Fast test: the committed report's header names the commit and tool versions of the committed goldens, and every relative change above 1e-3 in the report is listed in an 'accepted' section with an issue number; the fleet tests read the JSON instead of literals.

claim: The end-to-end chain on fleet geometry exists only in the aero tier. PR CI runs -m "... and not aero"; aero runs with the ci-full label or nightly. A broken binding between formulas on real geometry (a wrong applicability fact, a renamed input in the lateral chain) merges green and is found the next night.
evidence: pytestmark = [pytest.mark.aero]   # test_mvp_chain_fleet.py:25, same in every test_*_fleet.py of the chain
recommended_test: Fast tier, new aero_kernel/tests/test_mvp_chain_fast.py: BRYAN, CHEKKER (rudder only), BELEMNITOS (V-tail), RV-7 (flaps) and VOODOO (tailless) through evaluate(shipped_build(), aircraft_input(member), request(*SLUGS of test_mvp_chain_fleet + CORE_SLUGS of test_plan_batch_fleet), solvers=solvers_with(<fakes of formula_builders/asb_fakes>)). Assert per quantity the status (ok / not_applicable / the declared error code), the world keys {neutral-point=textbook, pappas, avl}, tool and application set, and for the pure-arithmetic nodes the hand value from the fake inputs (e.g. approach-speed = 1.3 x fake V_S; horizontal-tail-volume = S_h l_H / (S c) from the stand-in areas).

evidence: assert FleetMember.RV7.mass_kg == 0.500  # ... last mass asserted; PLAN_BATCH_MASS_KG covers the 28 plan models; no line for AVISTAR_ELITE / ULTRA_STICK_120

claim: No fleet test compares a kernel value with a measurement. Counted over the 17 fleet files: about 26 pure regression tests, about 40 relation/contract tests, 3 cross-checks against the CRRCSim prototype (same AeroSandbox), 0 flight-test or published values. The published Avistar Elite and FASER data are in the repository and unused.
evidence: MEASUREMENTS.md: "Nothing here is used by a test: the kernel marks no value as validated (A11), and the published values are coarse."
recommended_test: Aero tier, new test_validation_fleet.py, declared as a coarse bracket and not as validation of the method: stall-speed of AVISTAR_ELITE at 3.70 kg, sea level ISA, flaps 0, lies in [10.0, 13.0] m/s (published: mush at approximately 12 m/s at 3.70 kg and a stall break at approximately 14 m/s at 3.95 kg; the kernel gave 11.4 m/s on 2026-11-14); at 3.95 kg the value is larger by sqrt(3.95/3.70) = 1.033 within 1e-3 if C_L,max is unchanged, else within 2 %. Add the FASER values once MEASUREMENTS exist for ULTRA_STICK_120.

claim: The expected value is the production expression recomputed from the production outputs at 1e-12; a wrong closed form shared by test and code passes.
recommended_test: Replace the expectation's source, not the test: sample the fitted parabola C_D = C_D0 + k C_L^2 on a fine C_L grid (0.05..1.5, 1e-4 steps), take max(C_L / C_D) numerically and assert it equals max-lift-to-drag-probe within 1e-6; likewise oswald-efficiency == 1 / (pi k AR) with AR = b_ref^2 / S_ref from member.asb_reference.

claim: The stall goldens are 'pinned to their tools' by comparing provenance with whatever is installed, so an AeroSandbox upgrade is not named by this assert; the chain, plan-batch, neutral-point, tail-arm and roll files pin no version at all.
recommended_test: One shared constant GOLDEN_TOOL_VERSIONS = {'aerosandbox': '4.2.9', 'neuralfoil': '0.3.2', 'avl-binary': <installed pin>} in tests/reference_fleet.py and one helper asserting result.provenance.tool_versions against the subset that ran; call it in every *_fleet golden test.

claim: A relative tolerance of 2e-3 is applied to differences of AVL derivatives printed to six decimals: A6M2_ZERO's spiral-criterion-md is -3.74e-05 in the Pappas world, so the allowed deviation is 7.5e-08, below one unit of the last printed digit of its inputs. A harmless last-digit change (platform, AVL build) fails the test, and the doubling time derived from it (199.6 s) moves by percent.
recommended_test: Keep the tolerance for well-conditioned quantities; for spiral-criterion-* and spiral-doubling-time-* derive the tolerance from the print resolution: recompute the criterion from the recorded six-decimal derivatives of the same compute and assert equality to 1e-12, and compare against the golden with abs tolerance 2e-6 (two print units of a product of derivatives of order 0.1). State the reason next to the constant.

claim: Layout coverage of the fleet is narrower than its size suggests: 31 of 36 are conventional; the 2 flying wings pin unsupported_layout instead of a value; 4 of the 5 flapped aircraft (ALBATROS_4, GEE_BEE_R3, P39, SPIRIT_100) get no flap deflection, so their approach chain is recorded as upstream_failed; no aircraft has flaperons, elevons, a canard, two wings or twin booms. Defects in those branches (D9/D10 flaperon rules, Q35) are invisible to the fleet.
evidence: FLAP_DEFLECTIONS_DEG = {FleetMember.RV7: {"flap-deflection-takeoff": 15.0, "flap-deflection-landing": 30.0},}   # device roles in the 36 documents: elevator 33, rudder 27, aileron 25, flap 5, ruddervator 1, stabilator 1
